Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

1) What we heard:
- You're running a user-facing summarization + Q&A feature with strict hallucination targets (<5% on production prompts).
- Current vendor (MegaCorp) shows good latency but you flagged quality regressions on long, multi-turn threads and domain-specific prompts.
- Procurement wants a clear eval plan and artifact set to share with InfoSec.

2) Redwood differentiators (quick):
- Model quality: our eval on your seed prompts shows lower hallucination rates for entity recall and instruction-following cases (see attached CSV).
- Production controls: per-route fallback to verified model variant + automatic hallucination spot-checks integrated into the console.
- Cost/latency options: Dedicated pools with deterministic SLOs if you need committed throughput.

3) Proposed next tests (agree on order):
- Short smoke test (2k tokens total): reproduce your 10 representative prompts.
- Regression suite (50 prompts): check hallucination rate, factuality regression vs baseline.
- Adversarial spot-checks (10 prompts): prompts designed to provoke hallucination.

4) Ask from you: please confirm the 10 representative prompts (or give us a list) and whether we should include attachments to the procurement packet (SOC2 evidence is available on request).

I've attached the initial comparison CSV and the eval prompts we ran. If this plan looks good I can loop in our infra lead (Dev) to provision a short Dedicated pool for the regression run.

Thanks,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Thanks Sarah — quick answers inline and next steps.

> Can you confirm how hallucination is defined in that run?
We used the evaluation rubric you approved in the discovery call: a generated assertion is counted as a hallucination when it includes a verifiably incorrect factual claim (fabricated entities/relations) or when an entity attribute is confidently stated but contradicted by the reference. Partial/incomplete recall (omitting details) is tracked as an "omission" separate from hallucination. The CSV includes columns: prompt_id, reference, generated, hallucination_flag, omission_flag, confidence_score.

> SOC2 and data residency
We can provide the SOC2 report link and a short summary for procurement. For the regression suite runs we will keep data isolated to the provisioned Dedicated pool in our us-west region and we can produce audit logs for the test window.

Proposed timeline (if you confirm prompts):
- Fri 17 Jul: smoke test (your 10 prompts) on hosted Redwood and on a temporary Dedicated pool to compare latencies and metrics.
- Mon 20 Jul: full regression (50 prompts) with adversarial subset; Dev to provision Dedicated pool for 48h starting Mon morning.

Dev — can you confirm availability to spin up the Dedicated pool for Mon 20 Jul for ~48 hours? Please also run a regression that includes the hallucination spot-check script (attached) and export raw model outputs.

I'll attach the SOC2 link and the hallucination spot-checks in the next message for procurement.

—Marissa
